candidates.title: Q&A: Premier Danielle Smith says she doesn’t need Alberta separatists’ support
candidates.description: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith says she has told members of her party to back the province’s referendum results, or leave. In an interview with CBC’s West of Centre, she says she doesn’t need separatists to get re-elected.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 82 days later, no repairs started on washed-out road dividing small Quebec town
candidates.description: Residents in L’Ascension, Que., are still waiting on repairs after August flooding washed away part of their main road. The municipality's mayor blames the delay for repairs on the bureaucracy of different levels of government.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Duelling petitions highlight rift over paroled murderer at McGill law school
candidates.description: Students at McGill University's law faculty remain divided over the presence of a convicted murderer in the classroom, with a new counter-petition outlining why some students feel unsafe and don't want him in their presence.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The Marineland belugas keep dying. Was it a mistake to move them?
candidates.description: The deaths of six belugas at Marineland have raised questions about the impact of the transfers on their health and well-being and whether they were fit to travel. But was there ever a better option for the last captive whales and dolphins in Canada?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why Nova Scotia's AI data centre feels like a surprise reveal
candidates.description: Construction of Nova Scotia's new AI data centre in Point Tupper is well underway, yet so many people were surprised to learn about it. The CBC's Tom Murphy pieces together the timeline.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The RDSP was meant to help disabled Canadians save for the future. Yet many don't know it exists
candidates.description: The Registered Disability Savings Plan was intended to be a financial safety net for people with disabilities and the families who care for them. But it's only reaching about a third of those it was designed to help.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Will the Alberta referendum feed a more polarized immigration debate?
candidates.description: Beside Alberta Premier Danielle Smith's own political future, the most unresolved questions raised by her referendum concern immigration.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian privacy watchdogs powerless to hold Crime Stoppers accountable for data breach
candidates.description: In spite of a massive leak of Crime Stoppers tips revealed by a CBC investigation that a legal expert said could be "one of the worst breaches in Canadian history," both federal and provincial privacy watchdogs have suggested their hands are tied.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Rapid spread of fire was main factor in CFB Wainwright deaths, injuries: top military commander
candidates.description: The military's top commander believes the main reason soldiers couldn't escape the deadly fire at CFB Wainwright is because of how quickly it tore across the training area.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Inquiry looking into man's death in Edmonton ER hears about too many patients, not enough beds or doctors
candidates.description: An Edmonton physician says hiring more doctors won’t solve chronic overcrowding at Grey Nuns Community Hospital as the facility's five general medicine units have been operating above capacity.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New regulations on flags flown at Alberta schools to take effect in January
candidates.description: The Alberta government says new legislation about which flags can be displayed at schools will take effect in January. Those rules include making the Alberta and Canada flags mandatory, and prohibiting flags that "advance a social or political cause."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian women's rugby team scores 2nd straight win over powerhouse England
candidates.description: One loss isn’t a losing streak, but dropping two in a row is cause for concern. That’s exactly where the England Red Roses find themselves following Friday’s 31-22 setback in Ottawa, falling to Canada for a second time in the Rugby Rematch Tour of the WXV Global Series.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Chiefs, Opposition call for Alberta government to drop appeal of decision that quashed separation petition
candidates.description: With the Alberta referendum now in the books, some First Nation chiefs are calling on the provincial government to drop its appeal of a judge’s decision to quash the citizen petition on separation.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Loblaw CEO apologizes to 2 million shoppers for personal data hack, offers free credit monitoring
candidates.description: The CEO of Canada’s largest grocery retailer is apologizing to about two million shoppers for a data breach earlier this year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'I'm glad that he's gone': Winnipeg Jets fans say messy exit tarnishes Hellebuyck's legacy
candidates.description: Some Winnipeggers say Connor Hellebuyck can go to the Devils for all they care as Jets fans are ready to move past the trade saga.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Calgary family finds box of Pokémon cards valued at roughly $48,000
candidates.description: A Calgary family is giving thanks after they discovered an old box of Pokémon cards worth roughly $48,000 during Thanksgiving dinner.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Teen accused in girl's vicious attack in Quadeville pleads guilty
candidates.description: The teenager accused of a vicious attack on an eight-year-old girl in the tiny rural eastern Ontario village of Quadeville last year pleaded guilty to one count of aggravated sexual assault on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: It started with hockey, then he picked up a bat. Meet the Toronto catcher headed to the World Series
candidates.description: In just his second big league season, Toronto catcher Liam Hicks will make his World Series debut when the Tampa Rays take on the Milwaukee Brewers for Game 1 at 8 p.m. ET Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tens of thousands march in France as protests continue over schools and living costs
candidates.description: Clashes erupted in Paris as a mass march drew to a close Saturday, with more than 400,000 people rallying across France over school funding and soaring living costs in a fresh challenge to President Emmanuel Macron's government.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israelis are leaving the country in record numbers. Could a looming election accelerate the trend?
candidates.description: A record number of Israelis have left the country in recent years, data shows, and experts are raising the alarm ahead of a "watershed" election that they say could add to the trend and put more strain on the country's economy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why a new round in the U.S.-Iran conflict could be the most devastating yet
candidates.description: As the U.S. midterm elections approach, intelligence analysts warn that the United States and Israel are preparing for a devastating third round of direct military conflict with Iran. Experts caution that the region is locked in a dangerous, open-ended war of attrition.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Black Sea sailors thought a rescue boat was racing toward them. Instead, it was a drone that sank their ship
candidates.description: The Dignity is one of nearly 50 commercial vessels that maritime analysts say have been attacked in the Black Sea in October alone. The strikes are part of an escalating conflict that has brought much of the traffic through the key shipping corridor to a halt and prompted NATO to step up maritime security, including by deploying more patrol boats and radar.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Can millions of people live on the moon? These scientists say yes — but not for very long
candidates.description: Billionaires like Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos are claiming that we can expect big cities with millions of people on the moon, but a new study found that that may not be possible, so don’t start packing just yet.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney says 'direct casualties' are result of Ukraine's restricted access to Musk's Starshield
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Friday criticized a decision to restrict Ukraine's access to Elon Musk's military-grade satellite network, saying the move is costing lives.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump tells South Florida rally that U.S. warships could 'do a little stopover' in Cuba, after Iran
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday told a rally for candidates in South Florida that U.S. warships returning from the Middle East could stop over in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war, his latest suggestion of taking an interventionist approach to the nearby country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Netanyahu orders West Bank closure as Israeli soldiers, Palestinian gunmen killed in exchanges
candidates.description: The Israeli army says two soldiers were killed in an attack in the occupied West Bank on Friday that also left two Palestinian gunmen dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to order the closure of the territory.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Vivek Ramaswamy stands by ad featuring Amy Acton's mother despite bipartisan criticism in Ohio
candidates.description: Biotech billionaire Vivek Ramaswamy embarked on a statewide bus tour across Ohio with fellow Republicans on Friday, even as his gubernatorial campaign's ad featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Amy Acton was sowing growing divisions within his party as they fight to maintain political control of the state.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A polarized Brazil heads to presidential vote Sunday with economy, corruption top of mind
candidates.description: Frustrations around corruption and feelings of personal financial stagnation driving voting choices as Brazil heads to presidential run-off on Sunday, Oct. 25.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Melania Trump, Pope Leo broker humanitarian ceasefire for ravaged Ukraine city Oleshky
candidates.description: Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will ‌begin on Oct. 29, the White House said on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney defends doing business with countries that don’t share Canada’s values
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney defended his government’s pursuit of trade with countries accused of human rights abuses, arguing few nations meet Canada’s standards. Wrapping up a visit to Turkey, Carney insisted engagement does not equal approval, but declined to say whether he personally challenged President Erdogan over his government’s crackdown.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Europe's killer heat this summer claims record 50,000 lives, study suggests
candidates.description: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hundreds of flights cancelled, schools closed as Typhoon Champi hits Taiwan
candidates.description: Taiwan shut down schools and offices and grounded hundreds of flights as Typhoon Champi brushed by the island Friday, packing strong winds and torrential rains.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Elon, Starlink and the betrayal of Ukraine
candidates.description: SpaceX's Starlink service in Ukraine had its speed throttled recently, causing disruptions to their defense operations during Russian attacks. What does this reveal about big tech's role in modern warfare?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Searches of cellphones, laptops by U.S. customs up more than 32% so far this year
candidates.description: Searches of electronic devices such as phones and laptops of travellers entering the United States are up more than 32 per cent this year and are on track to set a new record, CBC News has learned.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tibet earthquake kills at least 16
candidates.description: A magnitude 7 earthquake hit China's Tibet region on Thursday evening, killing at least 16 people, injuring 46 and collapsing hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Execution staff warned of possibility some of Christa Pike's veins had 'blown': attorney
candidates.description: Tennessee execution team members failed multiple times to establish working IV lines in Christa Pike's arms before her attempted execution and warned that some of her veins may have ruptured, or "blown," before she was injected with the lethal drug, her attorney wrote in a court document filed Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Gisèle Pelicot and daughter join forces to empower victims of drugging and sexual assault
candidates.description: After a period of estrangement, Caroline Darian says she and her mother, Gisèle Pelicot, are "now, more than ever, together" as they launch a new public awareness campaign about drug-facilitated sexual abuse — also known as chemical submission.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump to swap some tariffs on Canadian goods amid midterm pressure
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump is poised to lift tariffs on some Canadian products — and hit others with new duties — as Republicans in border states lobby for relief from trade actions that have put them in a shaky political position ahead of November's midterms.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian planemaker Bombardier investing $270M in U.S. expansion
candidates.description: The company says its looking to hire for 500 roles and plans to add 300 more as it expands in Kansas, Indiana, Texas and Connecticut. U.S. President Donald Trump indicated the expansion was coming in a social media post on Thursday — after he walked back earlier threats to prevent Bombardier from selling in the U.S.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Consumer agency says unclear bank fees can add up for customers
candidates.description: Financial Consumer Agency of Canada says the bigger picture on how much Canadians pay in bank fees might be more murky than it should be, with foreign exchange fees and fees based on usage adding up for less wealthy Canadians in particular.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What is PHP, and how did a flaw in its code lead several websites to go dark this week?
candidates.description: PHP is an open-source computer language that powers an estimated 70 per cent of the internet. While websites being taken offline caused alarm, that was done to implement a fix — which cybersecurity experts say show the system for remedying such issues is working.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada Post starting weekend parcel delivery in Toronto, Montreal and Ottawa this fall
candidates.description: Canada's national mail carrier says it plans to start delivering parcels on the weekend to seven million households by the end of 2027, as part of the financially troubled Crown corporation's major restructuring.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge dismisses farmers' class action over end to Canadian Wheat Board monopoly more than a decade ago
candidates.description: A Manitoba judge has dismissed a class-action lawsuit seeking damages for grain farmers following the federal wind-down of the Canadian Wheat Board monopoly, marking what one expert calls the "last chapter" of the wheat board saga.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Palestinian families displaced as Israeli forces demolish Hebron homes, local officials say
candidates.description: The crackdown follows the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen on Friday - and comes just days ahead of Israel's election.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
candidates.description: Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to fight the blaze at the Nazi dictator's Alpine residence in Germany.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save
candidates.description: Kaylub Giamanco has been hailed as a hero for killing a teenager who fatally shot three children and a teacher.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
candidates.description: The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland
candidates.description: Three people - two women and one man - have been released, and one person remains in custody, gardaí say.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
candidates.description: She was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
candidates.description: The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests to form the biggest challenge to Vučić's rule.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
candidates.description: From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on some products, including certain machinery, and placed on others, such as carpets.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing
candidates.description: Police have launched a manhunt for the building's owner and contractor after the multi-storey building collapsed while still under construction.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump administration sues to block certification of upcoming Alaska election
candidates.description: The justice department has filed a lawsuit arguing that the inclusion of two candidates named Dan Sullivan could confuse voters.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Minneapolis withdrawal was 'surrender', Trump's ex-border patrol chief tells BBC
candidates.description: Greg Bovino was the public face of the controversial immigration enforcement operation in the city earlier this year.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: White House says Melania Trump brokered truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
candidates.description: Ukraine and Russia confirm the truce in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where residents have had to eat garden weeds to survive.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
candidates.description: Thirty-four people are also injured in the attack in southern Karak governorate, and a manhunt is now under way.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Argentina drops investigation into President Milei over crypto fraud
candidates.description: Javier Milei had denied acting fraudulently when a cryptocurrency nosedived after he deleted a social media post about it.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Deadly shooting near Paris is a 'racist terrorist attack', Macron says
candidates.description: One person is killed and five wounded in a series of attacks. The suspected gunman has been apprehended.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Freed US citizen was tortured in Russian jail, former Ukrainian prisoners say
candidates.description: Ukrainians held alongside the American say they witnessed beatings and sexual humiliation by Russian guards during his detention.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Who actually controls Ukraine's access to Starlink?
candidates.description: President Zelensky says limits to the technology continue to affect Ukrainian forces, while US officials and Elon Musk offer conflicting accounts of who controls it.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'It's part of the culture' - New York bans horse-drawn carriages after more than 160 years
candidates.description: The BBC's Madeline Halpert spoke to city tourists, residents and horse carriage workers about the industry and their opinion on the ban.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The rise of AI election ads in US midterms campaign
candidates.description: BBC Verify has tracked dozens of AI ads to assess how they are being used by campaigns in the midterms.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How Brazil's changing working class is reshaping the presidential race
candidates.description: Calls for change present a challenge to President Lula in the second round of the election on Sunday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ruins of Limoges city hall a symbol of France divided by national protests
candidates.description: Younger Limoges residents see the destruction of their town hall as unfortunate collateral damage in a wider movement. For others, the fire was an unacceptable tragedy.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Are California voters about to impose 'world's first' tax on billionaires?
candidates.description: Voters are about to decide if the mega-rich among them should hand over billions of dollars to pay for improvements to healthcare.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble
candidates.description: IT and cyber experts have told the BBC about their struggles in the last 48 hours to update their systems.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI
candidates.description: Indian workers are being paid to film themselves at work and the footage is used to train AI.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trains cancelled and road warnings as Scotland prepares for Storm Boelo
candidates.description: Heavy rain and strong winds are expected during the second named storm to hit in two days, with gusts of up to 80mph forecast.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Amber weather warning as Storm Boelo hits Scotland
candidates.description: The Met Office has issued an amber warning for wind over Scotland from 21:00 until 21:00 on Sunday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Storm Boelo to bring severe gales and heavy rain into Sunday
candidates.description: An amber weather warning has been issued for much of Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and northern England, as Storm Boelo approaches.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Weather warnings in place ahead of Storm Boelo
candidates.description: The amber Met Office alert for counties Antrim and Londonderry lasts from 21:00 BST on Saturday until 21:00 GMT on Sunday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The people on standby when a storm strikes
candidates.description: While most people are preparing to stay indoors as another storm approaches, others are getting ready to head straight into it.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Storm Austen brings power cuts and travel disruption as more wind and rain forecast
candidates.description: A second storm, Storm Boelo, is expected to hit Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England on Saturday bringing more wild weather.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Scotland to be hit with 80mph wind gusts as Storm Boelo warning upgraded to amber
candidates.description: It is due to be the second of two storms to hit Scotland over the weekend, with Storm Austen bringing heavy rain on Friday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: October's full Hunter's Moon to light up night sky this weekend
candidates.description: October's full Moon, known as the Hunter's Moon, will rise on Sunday night. Will the weather be in your favour?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Storm Austen hits UK as yellow wind warnings in effect
candidates.description: Disruption to travel is likely as the season's first named storm brings a swathe of powerful winds to south-west England on Friday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ukraine says Starlink is back to normal after disruptions
candidates.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that normal Starlink operating speeds were restored after more than a week of disruptions.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Gunmen open fire at a church during a funeral in Jordan, killing 7 and wounding 40
candidates.description: Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed three gunmen firing shots at a Greek Orthodox church in the city of Karak on Friday.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: European student protests take aim at Serbia's elections
candidates.description: Students have been protesting across Europe. In Serbia, they've selected candidates to run for parliament in Sunday's elections. And they're aiming to end 14 years of government by the populist leader Aleksandar Vucic.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Drinking water supplies dwindle in Yemeni city besieged by Houthi rebels
candidates.description: Taiz, a city in southwestern Yemen, faces a severe water crisis as Houthi rebels backed by Iran tighten their encirclement. The city has struggled with water issues for over a decade, but the situation has worsened in recent weeks.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Israeli PM pledges massive military operation after West Bank checkpoint attack
candidates.description: Israel's Prime Minister is vowing to launch a major military operation in the West Bank in response to an attack by two Palestinian gunmen on an Israeli military checkpoint that killed two soldiers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
candidates.description: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early
candidates.description: Military reinforcements are heading to the Middle East and some personnel have left the region, pointing to a potential attack on Iran. And, millions of Americans have already voted in the midterms.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Retired general discusses the U.S. and Israeli plan for possible attack on Iran
candidates.description: NPR'S Leila Fadel speaks with retired four-star Gen. Joseph Votel about the war in Iran and the U.S. and Israeli objectives for a potential post-election bombing campaign.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack
candidates.description: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Hacking attempts rise after flaws found in program affecting 70% of websites
candidates.description: Governments around the world are rushing to implement safety measures after AI technology found "severe" vulnerabilities in a key programming language called PHP.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A consultant is going viral for exposing the cringe-worthy DMs bosses send employees
candidates.description: A management consultant is going viral after he started sharing cringe-worthy anonymous DMs employees get from bosses. Like, ones they get on their wedding day and worse.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why Meta is charging to post more hyperlinks
candidates.description: Social media sites aren't the biggest fans of people leaving via hyperlinks. In fact, Meta has made it subscription-worthy for a Facebook Page to post more than two hyperlinks per month. What's the rationale for companies want to keep you on their site?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Gen Z is 'in the thick' of high housing costs. These candidates aim to solve it
candidates.description: Young candidates who rent or live with parents say their generation is "in the thick" of the country's housing affordability crisis. They argue this gives them new energy to solve it for everyone.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Americans can't get enough of mahjong. These traditional makers are cashing in
candidates.description: Shoppers in the U.S. are willing to spend hundreds of dollars for a mahjong set. In the eastern Chinese city of Taixing, manufacturers can barely keep up with the demand.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Is your Medicare Advantage plan ending next year? Here's what to know
candidates.description: Medicare open enrollment runs through Dec. 7, and for as many as 5 million seniors, it will be important to log on and pick a new plan.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Will a macaque eat a grape sitting on a pile of poo? A study on germophobia
candidates.description: When an outbreak strikes, humans try to avoid germs. (Remember wiping off groceries at the start of the pandemic?) What about ... monkeys?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why going on a 'say no' retreat is a gift to your future self
candidates.description: It's a day to think about all the upcoming appointments and commitments you're dreading — and then decline some of them. Writer Caroline Sylge shares a suggested schedule for the day.
candidates.author: NPR
